title: Potato Salad From Goldee’s With Secret Ingredient
description:
This potato salad recipe comes from 2024 Food & Wine Best New Chef Lane Milne of Goldee’s BBQ in Fort Worth, Texas. It’s a classic Texas barbecue side dish: thick and creamy with a crisp and refreshing texture from the celery and red onions, as well as the perfect amount of tang from cider vinegar, yellow mustard, and chopped dill pickles.
Recently, when scouring the internet and trying to plan a backyard barbecue menu, I came across one trick I hadn’t tried before: showering the hot potatoes with pickle brine.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 cup neutral cooking oil (such as canola)
3 pounds unpeeled Yukon Gold potatoes (about 12 medium potatoes)
1 tablespoon plus 1 generous pinch kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
4 scallions (light and dark green parts only), thinly sliced (about 1/2 cup)
1/4 cup finely chopped dill pickle, and juice separately
directions: Place potatoes in a large pot, and add water to cover. Bring to a boil over medium-high. Add a generous pinch of salt; reduce heat to medium, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the dressing: Place egg, vinegar, sugar, mustard, pepper, salt, and paprika in a blender or food processor. With processor running, slowly pour oil through food chute, and process until emulsified and creamy, about 1 minute. Season with additional salt to taste. Refrigerate until ready to use.

Drain and spread the hot boiled potatoes onto a cutting board, lightly smashing them with a fork, and sprinkling them with 3 tablespoons of Vlasic Kosher Dill Spears pickle brine before letting them cool completely, about 1 hour.

Stir in scallions, celery, onion, parsley, pickle, remaining 1 tablespoon salt, and reserved dressing. Season with additional salt to taste. Cover and chill until cold and flavors meld before serving, about 1 hour.
